title: Activation of Demand Response Programs Enrollments and the Enrollment Bonus
content:
## The rule

In the Demand Response Programs, an enrollment without a device requirement becomes active on its enrollment date. An enrollment with a device requirement becomes active when the device is installed and communicating, which must happen no later than the device installation period after the enrollment date. The period is counted in calendar days from the day after the enrollment date, and a device communicating on the last day is in time. An enrollment whose device is not installed in time lapses as unenrolled. The enrollment bonus is earned once on activation, and only for an enrollment in active status.

## Training questions and answers

**What starts the clock?** The enrollment date shown on the company's enrollment record. Day 1 of the installation period is the calendar day after the enrollment date.

**What is the installation period?** The program's device installation period, in calendar days: 30 for Smart Thermostat Rewards, 45 for the AC Cycling Program and 60 for Home Battery Dispatch. Peak Time Rebate, the Commercial Capacity Bidding Program and the Base Interruptible Program have no device requirement.

**Is the last day of the period in time?** Yes. A device that is installed and communicating on the last day of the period is in time; the comparison is "no later than" the last day.

**What if the device is installed and communicating after the last day?** The enrollment lapses as unenrolled; it does not become active.

**When does a program without a device requirement become active?** On its enrollment date.

**When is the enrollment bonus earned?** Once, on activation, and only for an enrollment that is in active status. An enrollment that lapsed as unenrolled never reached active status and earns no bonus. The bonus amount is the program's enrollment bonus; programs whose bonus is $0.00 earn nothing on activation.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Program | Hypothetical enrollment date | Last day of the period | Device installed and communicating | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Smart Thermostat Rewards (30 days) | June 10 | July 10 | July 10 | In time — active on July 10 |
| Smart Thermostat Rewards (30 days) | June 10 | July 10 | July 11 | Not in time — lapses as unenrolled |
| AC Cycling Program (45 days) | May 1 | June 15 | June 15 | In time — active on June 15 |
| AC Cycling Program (45 days) | May 1 | June 15 | June 16 | Not in time — lapses as unenrolled |
| Home Battery Dispatch (60 days) | April 5 | June 4 | June 4 | In time — active on June 4 |
| Home Battery Dispatch (60 days) | April 5 | June 4 | June 5 | Not in time — lapses as unenrolled |
| Peak Time Rebate (no device) | June 10 | — | — | Active on June 10 |

Counting the first row: June 11 is day 1; June 11 through June 30 are 20 days, and July 1 through July 10 are 10 more, so July 10 is day 30.

## Status words used on the enrollment record

- *Enrolled* — accepted and not yet active.
- *Active* — the enrollment has been verified and, where a device is required, the device is installed and communicating.
- *Unenrolled* — the customer cancelled before activation or left the program, or the enrollment lapsed because the device was not installed in time.
- *Removed* — the company ended the enrollment.
